title: Spicy Egg Ghee Roast Roll: A Mangalorean-Style Recipe That Beats Any Burger
excerpt: This protein-packed egg roll wraps Mangalorean ghee roast masala in a crispy Malabar parotta — a homemade cheat meal that takes under 30 minutes.
body:
• Mangalorean-style egg ghee roast wrapped in a flaky Malabar parotta makes a protein-packed cheat-day indulgence.
  • The recipe uses six boiled eggs tossed in a spice paste of dry-roasted coriander, cumin, fennel, mustard, and Kashmiri chillies blended with tamarind and yoghurt.
  • The ghee roast technique, which originated in Kundapur, Karnataka, produces a rich, tangy, and deeply aromatic masala that pairs with dosa, roti, or paratha.
  • The entire roll comes together in under 30 minutes once the eggs are boiled.

The ghee roast — a fiery, tangy, and richly spiced preparation from coastal Karnataka — has quietly become one of the most searched South Indian recipes on social media. Originally a Mangalorean chicken dish from the town of Kundapur, the technique has expanded to eggs, prawns, mushrooms, and paneer, making it accessible to a wider audience.

Content creator and chef Saloni Kukreja recently shared her take on Instagram: an egg ghee roast filling wrapped inside a crispy Malabar parotta to create a handheld roll that works as a satisfying cheat-day meal. The recipe uses six boiled eggs, delivering a generous protein hit, and swaps the usual takeaway burger or pizza for something rooted in Indian cooking tradition.

What Makes Ghee Roast Different

The defining move in any ghee roast recipe is the dry roasting of whole spices — coriander seeds, cumin, fennel, mustard, fenugreek, and Kashmiri chillies — before grinding them into a paste with tamarind pulp and yoghurt. The paste is then cooked in ghee until the fat separates, which concentrates the flavours and gives the masala its distinctive deep-red colour and nutty aroma.

Kashmiri chillies contribute colour rather than extreme heat, while tamarind and dahi balance the warmth with a sharp tanginess. Curry leaves, added to the sizzling ghee, provide the aromatic base note that runs through every bite.

Ingredients

  • 6 eggs, boiled
  • 3 Kashmiri chillies
  • 4 cloves of garlic
  • 2 tsp coriander seeds
  • 2 tsp cumin seeds
  • 1 tsp fennel seeds
  • 1 tsp mustard seeds
  • ¼ tsp methi (fenugreek) seeds
  • ½ tsp black pepper
  • 2 tbsp tamarind pulp
  • 1 tbsp ghee
  • 3 tbsp dahi (yoghurt)
  • Salt to taste
  • 8–10 curry leaves
  • ¼ tsp turmeric powder
  • ½ onion, sliced
  • 2 tbsp fresh coriander, chopped
  • 2 Malabar parottas (or roti of your choice)

Step-by-Step Instructions

  1. Boil the eggs for about 8 minutes. Transfer them to ice-cold water immediately to stop the cooking process. Peel and chop into medium-sized dice.
  2. In a dry pan, roast the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, fennel seeds, mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, black pepper, Kashmiri chillies, and garlic cloves until aromatic, about 2 minutes.
  3. Transfer the roasted spices to a blender. Add the dahi, curry leaves, and tamarind pulp. Blend to a smooth paste.
  4. Heat ghee in a pan over medium flame. Add the ground paste and turmeric powder. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring continuously.
  5. Add the diced eggs and mix well. Add a splash of water as needed, cover, and cook for 8–10 minutes until the masala thickens and the oil begins to separate.
  6. Stir in the fresh coriander and remove from heat.
  7. In a separate pan, cook the Malabar parotta on both sides until golden brown and flaky.
  8. Place the parotta flat, spoon the egg ghee roast masala down the centre, top with sliced onion and chopped coriander, and squeeze a lemon wedge over the filling.
  9. Roll tightly and serve immediately while hot.

Tips for the Best Results

Pricking the boiled eggs with a fork before adding them to the masala allows the spice paste to penetrate deeper. Using Byadagi or Kashmiri chillies keeps the colour vivid without overwhelming heat. For a richer version, Mangalorean cooks often add cashew nuts to the spice paste and a touch of jaggery for sweetness.

The roll format works particularly well for meal prep or as a portable lunch. The ghee roast masala can be made in a larger batch and refrigerated for up to three days, turning a weeknight dinner into a five-minute assembly.

"It combined a flaky Malabar parotta, perfect for a cheat-day indulgence, with a spicy, tangy, and buttery egg filling."

— Saloni Kukreja, content creator and chef

A Dish With Deep Roots

Ghee roast traces its origins to the Kundapur region of Karnataka, where it was traditionally made with chicken. Over the decades, the preparation has travelled across India and into diaspora kitchens. The egg version has gained particular popularity because of its simplicity — boiled eggs are forgiving to cook with, and the masala does most of the heavy lifting. Wrapped in a parotta and eaten by hand, it is the kind of Indian comfort food that rarely makes it onto restaurant menus but thrives in home kitchens and on food creator feeds.
